title: Quantum sensing for water-quality changes
subtitle: Classical simulation of proposed quantum sensing | 7 October 2026
body: 27.92% lower modeled total RMSE in an assumed 16-tap pilot
1.67× lower optical error at equal launched probe power
A dissolved-salt proxy calibrated from published optical data
Simulated feasibility; no claim of a deployed chemical detector
notes: Main results: results/summary.json. Sources and assumptions: docs/SOURCES.md. All concentration errors concern differential NaCl in mg/kg. Pilot assumes 100 m links, 10 nW/node, 1 s windows and 0.05 mK shared temperature residual.

title: The monitoring problem and our contribution
subtitle: Evidence for the need, a testable optical idea
body: UN 2025: only 60,000 of ~2 million reporting measurements came from poorest regions.
EPA: online monitoring supports treatment decisions and contamination investigation.
Proposed role: flag a mean salt-proxy change for confirmatory sampling.
Our addition: combine published CV sensing with water calibration, loss and drift tests.
notes: UN SDG Report 2025, Goal 6: https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2025/Goal-06/ reports approximately two million measurements used for reporting, 60,000 from poorest regions. These are monitoring data, not all worldwide measurements. WHO 2023 fact sheet, 2022 data: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/drinking-water . EPA online monitoring: https://www.epa.gov/waterresilience/online-water-quality-monitoring-resources . These sources establish importance and monitoring use cases, not a quantum bottleneck or salt-based pathogen detection. Operator need for this dose and sensitivity is an assumption. 16 taps is a design assumption: four binary splitter stages and Ns=1.6 below the 2.025 photons/mode cap. Not optimal or deployment-derived. Guo et al. demonstrated four nodes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09408 . Start with one/four measured taps. 100 m links, 10 nW/tap and 50 microkelvin residual are assumptions. Our contribution integrates existing CV theory with a NaCl proxy, losses, technical noise and decision analysis. No research-priority claim. docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md.

title: A measurable water proxy
subtitle: NaCl concentration changes are calibrated; pollutant identity remains unresolved
body: W is salt mass fraction. Around 500 mg/kg, dn/dc = 1.621 × 10⁻⁷ RIU per mg/kg.
Proposed 10 µm interaction length gives 6.570 × 10⁻⁶ rad per mg/kg.
YSI EXO field reference: salinity accuracy ±1% or 0.1 ppt; temperature accuracy ±0.01 °C.
Field accuracy bounds are not shot-noise standard deviations. This is a change detector, not a safety test.
notes: S7: https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.55.000947 Table 2, 298 K, 0–25% mass fraction. S11: https://www.ysi.com/product/id-599870/exo-conductivity--temperature-smart-sensor. Effective optical length and baseline are engineering assumptions. Practical salinity is not identical to NaCl mass fraction.

title: Implementation and measurement model
subtitle: Python on a CPU models a future squeezed-light instrument
body: NumPy models the Gaussian state; SciPy computes probabilities and constants.
pandas reads and writes CSV data; Matplotlib produces ten scientific figures.
Input: configuration, tap geometry and synthetic local concentration changes.
Calculate optical covariance, q̂ = Σ yᵢ / M, then optical and technical RMSE.
Compare coherent, independent squeezed and distributed probes at matched photons.
notes: Implementation evidence: src/model.py, src/run.py, src/validate.py, src/practical_comparisons.py and requirements.txt. Local Python 3.12.14 CPU execution. NumPy 2.3.5 arrays, covariance, seeded Gaussian draws; SciPy 1.18.1 constants and normal CDF, root solve in comparison helper; pandas 2.2.3 CSV processing; Matplotlib 3.11.2 PNG/SVG figures. Python unittest runs 13 internal model checks. Inputs: config/default.json and data/site_geometry.csv. Chemical concentrations in the trace are synthetic; coordinates only from supplied USGS-labelled file. Compute phase slope, loss, covariance, w^T Sigma w, add thermal/calibration variance, then threshold tests. Most RMSE curves are analytic. Monte Carlo: 100,000 null and alternative draws per strategy. A separate synthetic OU time trace has response lag. Seed 2601006. Outputs: results/summary.json, CSV, feasibility.npz, ten figures. Run bash src/reproduce.sh in project root with prepared .venv. No quantum SDK, circuit execution, ML training or quantum hardware. JavaScript/Node artifact-tool creates PPTX; Python creates offline HTML; Playwright prints PDF. Authoring tools are separate from the scientific simulator. Details: docs/SIMULATION.md. Theory: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10459 ; calibration https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.55.000947 .

title: Ideal scaling emerges from the model
subtitle: Lossless and uncapped: squeezed photons increase with M
body: Fitted exponent, M=33–64: classical −0.50; distributed −0.95.
This theoretical reference exceeds the practical 10 dB source cap.
notes: Computed by src/model.py and results/summary.json. Per-node squeezed budget 0.1 photon/mode, total Ns=0.1 M; equal launched bright-plus-squeezed photon budgets. S4 asymptotic displacement model.

title: Loss and drift soften the scaling advantage
subtitle: 100 m links, 10 dB source cap, 10 mrad phase jitter and 0.05 mK shared residual
body: More sensors add probe power. The quantum source reaches its cap at 21 nodes.
Curves describe differential precision under the specified engineering assumptions.
notes: results/scaling.csv, geometry=pilot. Assumed detector 95%, sample 90%, coupling 90%, 0.05 dB excess per splitter stage. Fiber 0.18 dB/km from Corning S9.

title: The 16-node pilot reduces total error by 28%
subtitle: One-second estimates, same 160 nW total launched probe power
body: Total RMSE: 0.092 → 0.066 mg/kg; 1.39× precision gain.
Independent squeezers reach 0.080 mg/kg: the distributed configuration adds a further 17% reduction.
notes: results/summary.json pilot16. No measured-field accuracy claim. Common residual 50 microkelvin is an ambitious compensated bench target.

title: Real distances reduce the regional gain
subtitle: 64 distinct supplied well locations; an assumed hub and 1.3× routing overhead
body: Locations span 3.5–16.6 km from the hub; mean transmission at M=64 is 37%.
At 64 nodes: 1.11× gain over optimized coherent power allocation.
The supplied file is USGS-labelled; missing provenance prevents independent field-data validation.
notes: data/site_geometry.csv derives coordinates only from draft. 8889 records reduce to 7704 coordinate pairs; nearest64 selected. As M changes, sampled population changes, so this is not a sensor-reduction claim for one fixed spatial target.

title: Temperature compensation determines useful gain
subtitle: Common thermal error appears in every sensor and survives spatial averaging
body: 1 mK corresponds to about 0.916 mg/kg of apparent salt change.
At a 10 mK common residual, quantum and classical total errors are almost identical.
notes: S10 reports dn/dT≈−1.485e−4 RIU/K at1550nm. The exact coefficient depends on temperature/composition. 0.05 mK and10 mK are assumed stochastic residuals, not manufacturer statistical specifications.

title: More classical light is a competing option
subtitle: Power sweep from 1 nW to 70 µW per node; no claim that water requires a 10 nW limit
body: ~28 nW/tap coherent matches the 10 nW/tap distributed total RMSE.
Same transducer and drift assumptions. The low-dose requirement needs justification.
notes: results/power_sensitivity.csv. 70µW is used only as a broad sweep endpoint comparable in magnitude to S1 detected probe power; S1 itself is a different wavelength/sensor. Pump and local-oscillator overhead are excluded from probe budgets. Derived by src/practical_comparisons.py; results/practical_comparisons.json.

title: Continuous averaging encounters slow drift
subtitle: Exact variance of a rectangular average of a 60-second correlated temperature process
body: Short windows are optical-noise limited; longer windows encounter correlated drift.
Fixed calibration offsets average across nodes, not across time. Long windows also blur fast events.
notes: docs/MODEL.md OU integrated-covariance formula. Stationary mean estimation, not transient tracking. Independent 0.03mg/kg node calibration offsets assumed.

title: Quantum readout improves a weak-change decision
subtitle: A 0.15 mg/kg regional increase; identical 1% false-alarm probability per decision
body: Detection rises from 24% to 47%; the same signal is easier to distinguish.
1% at 1 Hz means 36 expected flagged windows/hour. An operational alarm needs sequential validation.
notes: results/detection.csv. Independent Monte Carlo marginal windows, not independent samples of the OU trace. Assumes Gaussian moments including squeeze-angle jitter. Decision threshold is not regulatory. Bonferroni alpha=0.05/3600 bounds hourly familywise false-alarm probability at5% without independence.

title: Continuous monitoring of unequal local changes
subtitle: Synthetic arrivals differ across all 16 taps; the regional estimator remains well defined
body: The shared temperature trace and calibration realization are matched between strategies.
A 10-second response introduces lag. Stationary precision does not include this transient bias.
notes: results/time_trace.csv. Synthetic changes, not observed water data. Independent optical noise, common OU realization, seed2601006. Optical noise advantage concerns the aggregate; local contrasts do not receive the same benefit.

title: Sensor count and photon budget are distinct
subtitle: Fixed 160 nW total carrier-plus-squeezing budget and fixed total squeezing resource
body: Adding nodes spreads the same light more thinly; it does not produce a free 1/M improvement.
Sensor locations set coverage. Fewer sensors cannot guarantee the same protection against unsampled hotspots.
notes: results/resources.csv. Both total launched photon flux and total Ns fixed to16-node values in this panel. Component transmission includes stepwise splitter depth. Pump infrastructure not costed.

title: A real optical experiment anchors the opportunity
subtitle: Reported refractive-index sensitivities; a separate measured benchmark
body: 795 nm, air, 199 kHz ultrasound. *Best single-beam classical value is inferred in the paper.
Twin beams give 1.24× sensitivity gain over that best classical comparator; not a NaCl field test.
notes: Supplied quantum_photonic_sensing.pdf pp4–5, https://doi.org/10.1364/OPTICA.5.000628. Do not read sensitivity as 1-s Gaussian accuracy; no transfer of these RF numbers to our DC/telecom water scenario.

title: A credible next experiment
subtitle: Validate a four-tap optical prototype before extrapolating to a regional network
body: Calibrate NaCl phase response with standards and controlled temperature at 1550 nm.
Measure noise spectra, sample loss, modulation efficiency and squeezing at the same optical dose.
Compare coherent, independent squeezed and distributed readout using blind injected changes.
Validate drift, fouling and false alarms over hours; measure actual optical and electrical resources.
Advance only if total error improves. Keep chemical identification and spatial coverage as separate requirements.
notes: Proposed experimental plan, not completed hardware work. Four-tap size inspired by S6 laboratory demonstration. Existing simulation results are available in results/ and figures/.

title: Assumptions that control the result
subtitle: These are design targets, not measured specifications of a quantum water detector
body: 10 nW/node; 10 µm effective optical interaction; 500 mg/kg background; 1-second decisions.
10 dB maximum source squeezing; 1 MHz effective mode rate; 10 mrad phase-lock RMS.
95% detector, 90% sample, 90% coupling; 0.05 dB splitter excess/stage.
100 m pilot links; regional links = 1.3× geographic distance; 0.18 dB/km fiber anchor.
0.05 mK compensated common residual; 60 s correlation; 0.03 mg/kg independent calibration RMS.
10 mK field stress test; 1 nW–70 µW power sweep. Full register: docs/SOURCES.md.
notes: config/default.json is the single editable numerical configuration. All sourced versus assumed quantities are distinguished in docs/SOURCES.md. No costs, chemical selectivity or QML speedup are claimed. 16 taps is a design assumption: four binary splitter stages and Ns=1.6 below the 2.025 photons/mode cap. Not optimal or deployment-derived. Guo et al. demonstrated four nodes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09408 . Start with one/four measured taps. 100 m links, 10 nW/tap and 50 microkelvin residual are assumptions. Our contribution integrates existing CV theory with a NaCl proxy, losses, technical noise and decision analysis. No research-priority claim. docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md.
